articles.title: Suiza instala en un lago 1.400 paneles solares encadenados a pesas en el fondo: durante seis meses se vacía de agua y se anclan en una plataforma
articles.standfirst: Un proyecto de la empresa Romande Energie y que sería algo único en el mundo
articles.summary: Un proyecto de la empresa Romande Energie y que sería algo único en el mundo
articles.body: Los paneles solares parece que son el futuro de la humanidad, en cuanto a energía limpia se trata, son múltiples los proyectos que juegan con esta idea y uno de ellos ha instalado 1.400 placas en el lago de una montaña, a unos 1.810 metros de altitud. Se trata de la compañía Romande Energie y ha elegido el lago des Toules, un embalse alpino en Suiza, en el cantón de Valais, para crear un parque solar experimental que pasa la mitad del año posado sobre tierra firme, y la otra mitad elevado sobre el agua. A diferencia de los lagos naturales, este embalse hidroeléctrico se drena en determinados momentos del año, generando un cambio en el nivel del agua de hasta 15 metros. Para solucionar este problema, los ingenieros optaron por una estructura flexible: una plataforma de aluminio y polietileno que soporta 1.400 paneles fotovoltaicos bifaciales, encadenada a pesas que se sujetan en el fondo del lugar. Cuando el nivel baja por completo, la instalación se posa sobre el material diseñado para amortiguar el impacto, una vez vuelve a subir el nivel del agua, se mantiene funcionando de forma flotante, pudiendo ser usado durante todo el año. Estas son las principales dificultades que, desde Romande Energie, tuvieron que contemplar y sobrepasar para su parque solar:

articles.title: Raúl Varela: "Raphinha está a punto de convertirse en el mejor brasileño que ha pasado por el Barcelona"
articles.standfirst: El presentador de La Tribu defiende el impacto del delantero y lo sitúa por encima de Dani Alves, Ronaldo, Ronaldinho, Rivaldo y Neymar
articles.summary: El presentador de La Tribu defiende el impacto del delantero y lo sitúa por encima de Dani Alves, Ronaldo, Ronaldinho, Rivaldo y Neymar
articles.body: Raphinha vuelve a estar en el centro de los elogios. Raúl Varela puso sobre la mesa en La Tribu el impacto que está teniendo el delantero brasileño en el Barcelona y fue un paso más allá al compararlo con algunos de los grandes nombres de su país que han vestido la camiseta azulgrana. "Al debate le faltan cuatro goles mal contados para abrirse", comenzó Varela antes de recordar el recorrido de Raphinha desde su llegada al club: "Ese jugador llamado Raphael Días está a punto de convertirse en el mejor brasileño que ha pasado por el vestuario del Camp Nou vistiendo la camiseta azulgrana". Una afirmación de peso teniendo en cuenta la nómina de brasileños que han dejado huella en el Barcelona. Varela puso varios nombres encima de la mesa: Dani Alves, Ronaldo, Ronaldinho, Rivaldo y Neymar. "Y mira que hay competencia", señaló antes de repasar a algunos de ellos: "Los más de cuarenta títulos con un impacto descomunal de Dani Alves desde el lateral derecho, por supuesto los goles y la magia, aunque excesivamente concentrada en el tiempo de Ronaldo el Fenómeno y Ronaldinho, que duró tres telediarios en la élite. Me acuerdo de Rivaldo que fue totalmente determinante cuando se lo arrebataron al Depor y, claro está, Neymar que llegó a jugar, al menos, una temporada al nivel del mismísimo Leo Messi". Varela considera que muchos de esos futbolistas tenían mayores cualidades técnicas, carisma y repercusión mediática que Raphinha, pero eso no impide que el actual jugador azulgrana se haya convertido en una pieza fundamental: "Todos ellos jugadores imponentes, de mayores cualidades técnicas que el actual delantero de Flick, también con más carisma y foco mediático de este hombre de perfil bajo que sabe convivir a la sombra que proyecta Lamine". El director de La Tribu puso también el foco en los números y en todo aquello que aporta Raphinha más allá de los goles: "83 goles ya de culé y un montón de intangibles que le convierten en indiscutible, en líder y en capitán de un equipo que ha arrancado de forma sencillamente perfecta la temporada". Para Varela, el brasileño pertenece a esa clase de futbolistas que quizá no acaparan tanto foco fuera del terreno de juego, pero que resultan fundamentales para sus entrenadores: "Raphinha es uno de tantos de esa estirpe que no vende tantas camisetas como otros, ni firma tantos autógrafos. Pero a la hora de la verdad siempre encuentra acomodo en el once de su equipo sea en el puesto que sea porque tanto te fríe una corbata como te plancha un huevo". Y cerró su reflexión con una reivindicación contundente del brasileño: "Jugador apreciado y valorado por los de dentro, merece mayor reconocimiento fuera. Este Barça vuela porque el que bate las alas se llama Raphinha".

articles.title: Beaten by bias? Karnataka’s Krishik M misses Asian Games bus despite meeting AFI benchmark thrice
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: BENGALURU: They say truth is stranger than fiction — a lesson Karnataka’s top hurdler has just been handed the hard way.Despite clearing Athletics Fed.
articles.body: BENGALURU: They say truth is stranger than fiction — a lesson Karnataka’s top hurdler has just been handed the hard way.Despite clearing Athletics Federation of India’s (AFI) Asian Games qualifying benchmark not once but thrice, Krishik M still finds himself left out of the 110-metre men’s hurdles squad for the upcoming continental showpiece in Japan.The omission comes as a bitter blow to the 22-year-old BTech graduate — and to his father, Manjunatha, who gave up his job to support Krishik and his brother Kanishk in their pursuit of athletic careers.The AFI selection committee defended its decision pointing to the Inter-State meet in Bhubaneswar, where Krishik finished third – missing out on the federation's cutoff of a top-two finish.However, sources point towards a double standard, noting that the committee showed leniency to seasoned campaigners Tajinderpal Singh Toor (men’s shot put) and Annu Rani (women’s javelin throw) despite similar qualifying setbacks.Worse still, even after Tejas Shirse — the sole athlete initially picked for the men's 110-metre hurdles — withdrew from the Asian Games squad with an injury, the federation still didn’t call up Krishik.Krishik’s exclusion stands in sharp contrast to his performances throughout the season. Against the AFI qualifying standard of 13.63 seconds, the Tumakuru-native consistently delivered: 13.44 seconds (personal best) at the Indian Athletics Series (IAS) 6 in Chennai in early May; 13.52 seconds at the Senior Federation Cup in Ranchi later in May; and 13.55 seconds at the IAS 9 in Ludhiana in June.Reflecting on the setback, Krishik acknowledged his performance at the critical qualifying meet fell short. “I should have performed well at the Inter-State and secured at least a second position. Having said that, it’s only once in four years that we get an opportunity to represent India at the Asian Games,” he told TOI.When asked if his camp had appealed the decision, he added: “We did, but AFI insisted that I ought to have finished at least second at the Inter-State meet. I got three false starts in the final race. With even one foul, one comes under pressure, so I think that affected me.”Currently ranked seventh in Asia, the youngster remains focused on the immediate future. Looking ahead to the Indian Athletics Final Series in New Delhi today, Krishik remains defiant: “I'm 100% sure about winning and earning the qualification mark.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Correrá 900 kilómetros en 21 días... ¡para ver a Céline Dion en concierto!
articles.standfirst: La influencer Caroline Branaa iba a asistir al espectáculo de la cantante canadiense en 2020, pero se canceló, y ahora ideó este desafío para asegurarse tener las entradas
articles.summary: La influencer Caroline Branaa iba a asistir al espectáculo de la cantante canadiense en 2020, pero se canceló, y ahora ideó este desafío para asegurarse tener las entradas
articles.body: “Crecí con Céline Dion. Mis padres, mis tíos, mis tías, todos la escuchaban. Formó parte de mi infancia, de mi adolescencia, y aún lo es". La corredora e influencer Caroline Branaa es una admiradora de la cantante canadiense, a la que sigue desde su infancia. De hecho, tenía entradas para su concierto de 2020, que finalmente se canceló por la pandemia. Ahora, ante este nuevo espectáculo y antes incluso de que se pusieran a la venta las entradas, se fijó en otra influencer que ya tenía los tickets e ideó un reto: "Correré los 900 kilómetros hasta París si alguien me ofrece entradas", aseguró en su perfil de redes sociales. Poco después, la RTL (la emisora colaboradora del evento) se puso en contacto con ella en menos de 24 horas. Aunque ya tenía previstas otras carreras, como el maratón de París y el Hossegor Infinity Trail, empezó a preparar este desafío, pero el alto kilometraje hizo que tuviera que adaptar sus entrenamientos. "No sabía cómo prepararme para 900 kilómetros", admitía. "Al final lo he visualizado como una carrera de trail de 150 kilómetros y reorganizamos nuestro entrenamiento para que las carreras largas se acumularan, para que mi cuerpo entendiera que iba a afrontar largas distancias varios días seguidos. Mi carrera más larga fue de 80 km". La corredora saldrá de Hossegor este 12 de septiembre y dividirá el viaje en 21 días. El recorrido diario oscilará entre los 40 y 52 kilómetros, con un tramo final más corto para llegar algo más descansada. Pasará por Mimizan, Burdeos, Angoulême, Poitiers, Châtellerault y Orléans. Está previsto que llegue a la capital francesa el 2 de octubre... para asistir al concierto del día 3. "Mi la idea es descansar para poder disfrutar del concierto. No hay entradas para estar de pie, todos son asientos, lo cual es una suerte, porque Céline anunció un espectáculo de dos horas y estar de pie sería bastante duro"

articles.title: Inzaghi faces pressure at Al-Hilal as former Inter and Lazio coach struggles
articles.summary: Former Inter and Lazio head coach Simone Inzaghi is finding himself under increasing scrutiny in the Saudi Pro League, as pressure mounts following Al-Hilal’...
articles.body:
Former Inter and Lazio head coach Simone Inzaghi is finding himself under increasing scrutiny in the Saudi Pro League, as pressure mounts following Al-Hilal's disappointing 2-0 home defeat to Neom Sports Club.

The Italian coach, who made the high-profile move to Riyadh after departing San Siro, was met with heavy booing from the home supporters at the final whistle. The defeat marked a fresh low point in an unsettling start to the campaign, with disgruntled fans taking to social media to campaign for his dismissal under the hashtag #InzaghiOut.

According to Calciomercato.it , the atmosphere surrounding the Piacenza-born coach has grown increasingly tense as the Riyadh giants struggle to match expectations.

NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE – JUNE 26: Simone Inzaghi Manager of Al Hilal during the FIFA Club World Cup 2025 group H match between Al Hilal and CF Pachuca at GEODIS Park on June 26, 2025 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Richard Pelham/Getty Images)

Latest Al-Hilal defeat sees pressure mount on Inzaghi

The defeat to Neom, who have invested heavily to compete in Saudi Arabia 's top flight, has intensified criticism regarding Inzaghi 's tactical setup and recent team performances.

Despite the growing online backlash and vocal frustration from the stands, the Al-Hilal hierarchy has not yet issued any official statement regarding the 50-year-old's future.

However, with expectations at the Asian champions notoriously high, Inzaghi is under immediate pressure to reverse the club's fortunes in their upcoming fixtures to avoid an early exit from his Middle Eastern venture.

articles.title: Texas Longhorns LB Rasheem Biles earns SEC honors
articles.summary: Rasheem Biles is already making headlines. The talented linebacker was named the Southeastern Conference's Co-Defensive Player of the Week.
articles.body:
Just one game into his Longhorns career and Rasheem Biles is already making headlines. The talented linebacker was named the Southeastern Conference 's Co-Defensive Player of the Week on Monday, following a stellar performance against Texas State . In his first game in the burnt orange, Biles showed why he is a special player.

Against the Bobcats, Biles recorded five tackles with a half tackle for loss and forced two turnovers. His turnovers were a forced fumble and an interception that helped keep the momentum with the Longhorns . While the offense scored nearly 60 points, the defense showed it is a force to be reckoned with, with Biles leading the way.

As the Longhorns held Texas State to 349 yards of total offense, Biles was one of the team's best players. He finished third on the team in total tackles and was tied for first on the team in tackles for a loss. Regardless of the matchup, he made life difficult for the Texas State offense all afternoon.

On Saturday, he flashed the form that made him a star at Pittsburgh. He finished his Panthers career with 183 total tackles and 10.5 sacks. In his last season in the ACC, Biles set career highs in tackles with 100 and assists with 61. That is partly why he was a popular target in the portal.

For the Longhorns, Biles' successful debut was a welcome sign. He is expected to be a key piece of the defense and will be counted on against some of the country's best teams. If Biles can continue to build on his performance from the season opener, then more weekly awards will be on the horizon.

articles.title: Could Rally Chile offer Adrien Fourmaux the best chance at elusive WRC win?
articles.summary: Fourmaux now faces “a very good opportunity” to claim his first win in rallying’s top tier
articles.body:
After driving "as good as he's ever driven" in Paraguay, Rally Chile could present Adrien Fourmaux "a very good opportunity" to claim a maiden World Rally Championship victory, according to Hyundai Motorsport .

The Frenchman has been knocking on the door of an elusive first WRC win. The Hyundai factory driver came close in last year's Saudi Arabia season finale, however a check-in error while leading the event forced Fourmaux and co-driver Alex Coria to settle for second.

This year, Fourmaux has often led the Hyundai charge in terms of outright pace. A second place at Safari Rally Kenya came after losing more than two minutes on the opening stage.

Last time out in Paraguay, Fourmaux was again in the victory fight before punctures provided a setback. The 31-year-old, however, produced a head turning performance to fight back to third, after taking a minute out of the front runners, ending the rally with nine stages wins. Fourmaux declared after the rally that he felt he "deserved the victory".

Impressed by the drive in Paraguay, Hyundai sporting director Andrew Wheatley is convinced a first win will arrive sooner or later and believes this weekend's outing in Chile could provide an opportunity.

Adrien Fourmaux was in the fight for victory last time out

"It's [the first win] going to happen. There's no question," Wheatley told Motorsport.com. "He's now addressed and identified all of the challenges that were keeping him off the top step. I think his performance in Paraguay was about as good as he's ever driven.

"The reason why I say that is because his performance was consistent. Where he's making a positive impression at the moment is he drove every stage at a 100% and that's difficult to do, particularly in those challenging conditions.

"But that's how you win rallies by being consistent and consistently performing at a high level. And I think you know he's mentally pretty strong at the moment. I think it'll be a bit like Sami Pajari , who has won his first three WRC victories back-to-back [this year]. Once he can get that win off his shoulders, it will flow a lot easier.

"In terms of pure pace, we saw it earlier in the year in Safari where he dropped two minutes and 15 seconds on the first stage and finished second by 25 seconds. So that was annoying.

"Paraguay was equally annoying because he dropped around about three minutes with punctures and little problems over the weekend and again was able to take a minute out of Elfyn [Evans]. On Saturday, taking a minute out of a guy that's fighting for the world championship and a minute out of Sami as well is difficult.

"I believe the win is coming. I think this is probably a very good opportunity. He was fast here last year but if he can have the same rhythm that he had in Paraguay here, I think he could be ready to fight for a win."

Andrew Wheatley (left) believes a first win is coming for Fourmaux

Fourmaux showcased his speed in Chile last year after enjoying a spell in the lead before eventually finishing in third.

This weekend's event is expected to be largely dry, but the stages will be abrasive in places offering a high puncture risk. Crews will however have eight extra tyres at their disposal following a change in the regulations.

Road sweeping is also likely to be a factor, meaning road position will be crucial. Fourmaux will begin the rally from fifth on the road.

"I'm really looking forward to Rally Chile after showing very strong pace throughout the weekend in Paraguay – it gives us confidence and hopefully we can carry this performance into Chile," said Fourmaux.

"It's a rally I really enjoy, last year we were fighting at the front, and we finished on the podium. The stages are fast and flowing, but also quite technical, so you need a lot of precision and confidence in the car. We know we were competitive there last year, and after the performance we had in Paraguay, the target is to fight at the front again and push for the best possible result."

articles.title: Stuttgart reportedly extend contract of talented 18-year-old academy striker
articles.summary: As reported by the Stuttgarter Nachrichten, Enis Redzepi has signed a new contract that ties him to VfB Stuttgart until 2028. According to the local newspape...
articles.body:
As reported by the Stuttgart er Nachrichten, Enis Redzepi has signed a new contract that ties him to VfB Stuttgart until 2028.

According to the local newspaper, there is also an option for the talented attacker to extend his deal for a further season.

Redzepi has made seven appearances so far this campaign for Stuttgart's U-19 team, netting an impressive tally of twelve goals.

Just like Ermedin Demirović , the 18-year-old also scored a hat trick in yesterday's 5-0 win in the UEFA Youth League against Viking FK.

Kicker.de is already comparing Redzepi to one of the best Stuttgart strikers in the club's history in the form of the legendary Mario Gómez .

Just like the 78-cap ex-German star, Redzepi came through the Sweabian's youth academy and could soon be part of the U-23 team.

He even made his 3. Liga debut last Sunday as a second-half substitute in their 2-1 victory against Würzburger Kickers.

articles.title: Kentucky vs Alabama: Offensive X-Factors in week two
articles.summary: With Alabama coming to Lexington for a conference clash with Kentucky, we take a look at offensive X-factors in what could be a high scoring game.
articles.body:
Kentucky football hosts the Alabama Crimson Tide on Saturday for a massive SEC home opener. The Wildcats will be home underdogs and will try to shock the world by getting just their third ever win in the series. This might be a high scoring, shootout type of game, as both offenses are capable of big plays and scoring in bunches.

In this article, we will go through offensive X-factors for both teams and what to expect this weekend and what to expect on the offensive side of the ball. Let's take a look at some key players.

Kenny Minchey had a phenomenal debut in week one against Youngstown State in his first college start, now he gets his first SEC start against one of the best secondaries in the country. Minchey played a clean game in week one, and his operation of the offense did not look like a player making his first start. The offensive scheme will create misdirection and get playmakers open on this Alabama defense. I think a large part of this game comes down to which quarterback is more comfortable and consistent throughout the game.

Kentucky has a stable of tight ends that are difference makers, and they need to lean on them in this game. Willie Rodriguez had a team-high six targets in week one and will constantly be a threat to make plays in the passing game. Kentucky has two big outside receivers in Nic Anderson and DJ Miller, but they have a tough matchup against the corner duo of Zabien Brown and Dijon Lee. This tight end group can create mismatches in the passing game like we saw in week one, and I expect a ton of 12 and 13 personnel from Kentucky to get multiple tight ends on the field at the same time.

Rodriguez is the do-it-all tight end, but Skinner is a true X factor move tight end that has incredible athleticism. They will continue to find ways to get Skinner the football in space and he can showcase that athleticism. Skinner is tough to defend in open space and has a large catch radius. I expect the offense to lean on Rodriguez and Skinner in the passing game, and they will also help get the run game going in these two or three tight end sets.

Keelon Russell had a solid debut and will get the first SEC road start of his career on Saturday. He has to stay poised and make plays from the pocket, but as he showed in week one, he has the ability to extend plays with his legs which is something the Kentucky defense has to be aware of. Russell needs to play better than he did in week one for the Crimson Tide to get the win, and he has to lean on his dynamic playmakers. In a lot of ways, I truly think this game comes down to which quarterback can consistently play in rhythm and take care of the football.

Ryan Coleman-Williams had five catches for 130 yards in the season opener against ECU, but he still had a couple drops and had a few reps where the effort was lacking. Coleman-Williams has the potential to take the game over and will see a large target share on Saturday. Alabama needs the best of Coleman-Williams in Lexington this weekend, and there will be plenty of opportunities for him to make plays. The run game for the Crimson Tide remains a bit of a question mark, and if they can't get that going they will need to lean on the passing game.

articles.title: FPL: Justin a great differential pick?
articles.summary: Leeds have teamed up with Fantasy Football Scout to help bring you hints, tips and advice during the 2026/27 Fantasy Premier League (FPL) season. Scout will...
articles.body:
Leeds have teamed up with Fantasy Football Scout to help bring you hints, tips and advice during the 2026/27 Fantasy Premier League (FPL) season.

Scout will be using their expertise to provide advice and gameweek tips which should prove useful in ensuring you win your mini-leagues.

Jayden Bogle (£4.5m) was Leeds' top FPL points scorer in Gameweek 3. The full-back scored and picked up all three bonus points in the draw away at Brighton & Hove Albion. The defender also registered the four clean sheet points as he was substituted ahead of the Seagulls' goal.

Bogle has now returned 22-points in the opening three matches of the season. He is the fourth highest scoring defender in the game, with only the Hull defenders, who have kept three clean sheets, out scoring him. The 26-year-old is currently averaging 7.3 points per start in FPL, making him incredible value for money.

Midfielder Tanaka Ao (£4.9m) made his first Premier League start of the season in that encounter on the south coast. The Japanese international assisted Bogle's goal, meaning that he returned five points in Gameweek 3.

Defensive trio James Justin (£4.5m), Tarik Muharemović (£5.0m) and Nico Elvedi (£4.5m) all achieved the defensive contributions threshold in Gameweek 3. All three were rewarded with the two additional Defensive Contribution points in the game as a result. Justin and Elvedi registered 10 defensive contributions each, the exact number needed to receive the additional points. Muharemović registered an impressive 13 defensive contributions.

Defender Justin has made an excellent start to the season and has already shown the potential for returns at both ends of the pitch.

Only Bogle and Anton Stach (£6.0m) have registered more FPL points than the England international in the Leeds team so far this season. Justin's 16 points have come from a clean sheet, two lots of Defensive Contribution points, two bonus points as well as six appearance points.

Over the course of the opening three matches, the versatile full-back has registered 30 defensive contributions. This is 13th across all of the defenders in the game. In the Leeds team, only Muharemović has made more with 39.

Justin has also shown attacking threat in the opening three weeks of the season. The defender has supplied five crosses, only Stach and Harry Wilson (£6.4m) have crossed the ball more in the Leeds team. He has also had three shots, of which two have been on target, and he has created a chance for his Leeds teammates.

Crystal Palace's Tyrick Mitchell (£4.5m) was the top scorer in Gameweek 3. Mitchell scored twice and registered two bonus points on his way to a 15-point return in FPL. The budget-friendly left-back registered just one-point more than Leeds' own Bogle who was the second highest scorer with 14.

Liverpool's Alexander Isak (£9.0m) had been a popular sell with FPL managers heading into Gameweek 3. Over 260,000 managers sold the forward and he punished them with 13 points courtesy of his two goals and all three bonus points. Isak's teammate Cody Gakpo (£7.1m) also had a good week. Gakpo assisted both of Isak's goals for an 11-point FPL haul. The Dutch forward is currently the top scoring player in the game.

Like Gakpo, Brentford's Vitaly Janelt (£5.0m) also registered 11-points in Gameweek 3. Janelt scored and registered 12 defensive contributions which was enough to earn him the extra two Defensive Contribution points. He now has two goals, four Defensive Contribution points, a clean sheet point and three bonus points in the opening weeks of the season. The only team he failed to return against was the Whites!

articles.title: 🎧 Foxes' new low & was Duff's Wycombe sacking harsh?
articles.summary: Listen to the latest episode of BBC's 72+ podcast with Aaron Paul, Bristol City winger Jed Wallace and AFC Wimbledon boss Johnnie Jackson.
articles.body:
Aaron Paul is joined by Bristol City winger Jed Wallace and AFC Wimbledon boss Johnnie Jackson in the latest episode of the 72+ podcast.

They discuss what's next for Leicester City and Russell Martin after the Foxes were thrashed 4-0 at home by Oxford United last weekend to leave them 18th in League One.

Jackson reflects on Wimbledon's start to the campaign and Michael Duff's sacking at Wycombe Wanderers after just five games - with the Chairboys 23rd in the third tier - is also a topic of conversation.

articles.title: Report: Manchester United send scouts to watch Champions League forward
articles.summary: Manchester United Tracking Nicolo Tresoldi as Tottenham Rivalry Builds After Club Brugge Scouting MissionManchester United’s recruitment team were back on th...
articles.body:
Manchester United Tracking Nicolo Tresoldi as Tottenham Rivalry Builds After Club Brugge Scouting Mission

Manchester United's recruitment team were back on the road this week, and the trip to Belgium may yet prove significant. According to TeamTalk , United and Tottenham both sent representatives to watch Club Brugge forward Nicolo Tresoldi on Tuesday evening, with the 22-year-old increasingly viewed as one of Europe's standout emerging attackers.

Tresoldi was on the scoresheet from the penalty spot in Brugge's 3-2 defeat to Aston Villa , and that appearance offered another timely reminder of why interest is building. TEAMtalk states that "Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur both had representatives in Belgium on Tuesday evening to watch Club Brugge striker Nicolo Tresoldi", underlining the level of attention now surrounding the German Under-21 international.

Nicolo Tresoldi emerging on Manchester United shortlist

This was not a one-player visit from United either. The report adds that the club "also used the trip to continue their work on left-back Joaquin Seys ", a player they had previously explored during the summer. That points to a broader Club Brugge assessment, though Tresoldi appears to be the name drawing the sharpest focus.

He arrives in this conversation with encouraging numbers and strong momentum. "He scored 23 goals last season", and those returns help explain why "his performances sparked considerable interest across the continent, with Barcelona among the clubs to hold talks over a potential move." Brugge managed to retain him, but the sense from this latest development is that his situation remains under close review.

Tottenham also pushing hard in Tresoldi race

Tottenham are firmly in the frame as well. TEAMtalk reports, "We can confirm Tottenham were also in Belgium to carry out further work on Tresoldi, who remains high on their radar." With Roberto De Zerbi looking to reinforce his attacking options, the striker is described as a player who "could develop into a strong option for the club."

That makes this one worth monitoring, particularly because both clubs have clear reasons to be active in the market. United "failed to add a forward over the summer and continue to assess attacking options for the future." There is also a notable line on Joshua Zirkzee , whose "future at Old Trafford remains in doubt after failing to force his way into Michael Carrick's starting XI."

Club Brugge talent offers flexibility for future planning

Perhaps the most revealing part of the report is the practical framing around United's next move. "United's position on the Dutchman remains the same – they won't let him go without first signing a replacement. Tresoldi could be that player." That is not the same as an imminent bid, but it does place the Brugge striker squarely in the thinking.

There is a wider picture too. Tresoldi "has rapidly established himself as one of the most exciting attacking prospects in Europe" and, if current form continues, "it seems only a matter of time before Tresoldi makes a high-profile switch to one of Europe's top sides." For now, the scouting stage continues, but both Manchester United and Tottenham appear to be gathering for a serious contest.

From a Manchester United perspective, this feels like the kind of move that makes a lot of sense if the club are planning carefully. Nicolo Tresoldi does not yet arrive with the noise of a finished superstar, but that can often be where the smartest recruitment lives. If United are genuinely looking for a forward with upside, athletic potential and room to grow, then this is exactly the profile they should be studying in detail.

The mention of Joshua Zirkzee is what really sharpens the debate. If the club "won't let him go without first signing a replacement", then United need to be absolutely certain on the next option. Tresoldi's numbers are promising, and the fact both United and Tottenham were there suggests he is being taken seriously at a high level. That alone raises the stakes.

There is also something encouraging about United doing multiple pieces of work in one trip, including Joaquin Seys. It hints at joined-up planning rather than opportunism. Supporters have wanted a more coherent recruitment model for years, and identifying players before the whole market explodes around them is part of that.

The obvious question is whether Tresoldi is ready for the pressure and physical demands of Old Trafford. That is where the scouting process matters. Watching him live, checking how he moves, how he reacts, how he influences a game beyond goals, all of that is crucial. On the face of it, this report is intriguing. United need more attacking certainty for the medium term, and Tresoldi sounds like a player worth serious attention.

articles.title: “We’re Both Fiery”: Caitlin Clark Opens Up About Angel Reese Before Team USA’s Quarterfinal Against Hungary
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese have completely flipped the script overseas. Everyone expected Caitlin Clark and her biggest rival to cause massive drama insid...
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese have completely flipped the script overseas. Everyone expected Caitlin Clark and her biggest rival to cause massive drama inside the locker room. Instead, the two generational rookies have joined forces to absolutely dominate the international competition together. They are currently leading the American squad into a highly anticipated knockout-round match against Hungary.

Fans absolutely love seeing these two superstars finally sharing the same jersey. Their on-court chemistry has been completely electric throughout the entire group stage. Caitlin Clark has been throwing ridiculous highlight passes right into the paint for easy buckets. Reese cleans up every single rebound and provides insane physical energy on the defensive end.

The Indiana guard recently sat down with reporters to talk about playing alongside her biggest career rival. She did not hold back her praise when describing what makes the talented forward so successful. Giving massive respect to her teammate, she dropped the exact headline quote.

She noted, "We're both fiery" when chasing basketball championships.

Seeing two massive competitors put aside their personal battles for the national squad is super refreshing. True basketball fans know that elite players respect anyone who matches their intense competitive energy. Caitlin Clark looks completely comfortable sharing the massive international spotlight right now. The American roster is firing on all cylinders as they push toward another gold medal.

Caitlin Clark, Team USA, Prepares For Brutal Knockout Bracket Matches

The national team coaching staff definitely found the ultimate cheat code by playing the rookies together. Head coach Kara Lawson loves the intense hustle the young core brings to the floor every night. Caitlin Clark actually dropped a second quote to praise her teammate's work ethic. She pointed out that Reese "has a tremendous motor" compared to anyone else.

While the American squad cruised through the group stage undefeated, the competition is about to get significantly tougher. They barely survived a massive scare against Italy earlier in the tournament. That specific wake-up call proved that nobody can simply coast through these brutal international brackets. Caitlin Clark knows the margin for error drops to zero once the quarterfinals begin.

If they handle business against Hungary, a ridiculously tough matchup against either Spain or Australia waits in the semifinals. But the biggest looming threat is definitely the French squad. France is currently dominating the power rankings and looking for major revenge. The Americans need perfect execution to keep their massive tournament win streak alive.

At this point, proving they can play together is old news for the young superstars. Caitlin Clark and the rest of the crew just want to secure another championship for the program. The dynamic rookie duo has a serious chance to show the entire world how dangerous their chemistry really is. Expect them to come out swinging, pare.

articles.title: Celtics Star Jayson Tatum Reveals How 2025 Injury Change Him, Commemorates It Through His New Shoes
articles.summary: The 2025-27 season might be the worst in Jayson Tatum‘s career. He was not able to play much, and his team suffered one of the most painful playoff losses fo...
articles.body:
The 2025-27 season might be the worst in Jayson Tatum 's career. He was not able to play much, and his team suffered one of the most painful playoff losses for any player or team — blowing a 3-1 lead in a seven-game series.

Much of the blame is on the Boston Celtics forward's injury in the second round of the 2025 playoffs.

The Celtics faced off against the New York Knicks in the Eastern Conference semifinals, but their fate changed drastically when Tatum got injured in Game 4. It was a career performance for the six-time All-Star. He already had 42 points, eight rebounds, four assists, four steals, and two blocks under his name.

Unfortunately, he suffered an ACL injury in the final minute. It was eventually ruled a season-ending injury. The Celtics were eliminated in six games.

The 2017 No. 3 pick eventually returned in March, and the Celtics were among the best teams at that time, thanks in large part to Jaylen Brown , who was having an MVP-caliber season.

Tatum has been vocal about how traumatized he felt by that experience. He once discussed how he felt scared about returning to Madison Square Garden, where he suffered the injury.

"Nervousness, anxiousness, all the things you'd probably expect from the last time I played here. But it's a game," he said back in March.

Jayson Tatum still remembers the feeling

Six months into his successful return from the injury, Tatum admits that the event still haunts him. He confessed that he feels different because of the injury.

He will forever remember that painful moment, as he now commemorates it with his new shoe line. He released the Jordan Tatum 5, which he said was designed with his past injury in mind .

"On every Tatum 5, on the right side, there are five lines across the heel just to acknowledge the scar on my right heel," he during an event to launch the shoes (via Complex).

"What I've had to learn and also accept from that experience is, anytime you go through something traumatic, you're not the same you. You just can't be the same person anymore. And that's not saying that you're any worse, you're just different…So, aligning that with the Tatum 5, it looks different than every other shoe (I've had)."

Tatum will now head to the next season healthier and with bigger responsibilities as the team's lone star, following the shocking trade of Jaylen Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers .

articles.title: Moreno Vs. Morales Odds, Full Fight Preview & Prediction
articles.summary: Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) Flyweight standouts Brandon Moreno vs. Joseph Morales will collide this weekend (Sat., Sept. 12, 2026) inside Desert Dia...
articles.body:
Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) Flyweight standouts Brandon Moreno vs. Joseph Morales will collide this weekend (Sat., Sept. 12, 2026) inside Desert Diamond Arena in Glendale, Ariz., for Noche UFC 4 .

At 32 years of age, it feels like the best days of "The Assassin Baby" are behind him. That shouldn't be a shock given he's been fighting professionally for 15 years and 35 fights, but he's struck by an unusual case of inconsistency. Sometimes, Moreno still has the sharpened look of a champion, whereas other bouts see him falling over himself while loading up haymakers.

Either way, he's lost two straight leading to this co-main event versus red-hot Morales. "Bopo" was an unfortunate victim of the halfway Flyweight division dissolution of 2018 , and it took seven years for the prospect to return to the Octagon via The Ultimate Fighter (TUF) . Fortunately, two dominant victories via stoppage prove that Morales is back better than ever, and he's looking ready to make a run at gold.

Let's take a closer look at the betting odds and strategic keys for each athlete:

As mentioned in the intro, Moreno can be a frustrating fighter to watch. At his best, he can strike with anybody and possesses the division's best jab, as well as punishing kicks and counters. He doesn't have to just marching forward swinging loopy overhands, and yet that's what he does half of the time. Standup woes aside, Moreno is a slick grappler with strong wrestling.

What we have here is a good old-fashion collision of Mexican boxers that just so happens to take place inside a fenced cage. Sure, both Moreno and Morales are jiu-jitsu black belts, but they win a lot of exchanges and often bring fights to the floor via their boxing prowess. If you like matchups where mixed martial arts (MMA) fighters actually stand their ground and trade combos, this may end up as your " Fight of the Night. "

What's the most important weapon in a boxing match? The jab. What does Moreno neglect to utilize in most of his losses? The very same jab. Against Morales — a combination puncher with a powerful right hand — Moreno has to make use of his range advantage and continually pepper "Bopo" to interrupt his offense.

If Moreno's jab is flowing, everything tends to work well for the former champion.

Morales is a well-rounded athlete who specializes in boxing and jiu-jitsu. From top or bottom position, "Bopo" is really slick and able to wrap up submissions quickly. Despite having just two knockout wins on his record, Morales can crack as well, scoring plenty of his finishes via club-and-sub.

This is a matchup of boxers, and given the grappling/anti-wrestling prowess of both men, it feels likely to stay on the feet. In his UFC return versus Alibi Idiris , Morales found great success with consistent pressure, combinations, and body work. Against a brick-chinned vet like Moreno, he should also be trying to control the center and hit the midsection.

Moreno's recent losses have demonstrated a vulnerability to low kicks, and boxing exchanges should further expose his lead leg. I'd love to see Morales actively attacking the calf as a counter to jabs, as well as a punctuation mark to his combinations. If Morales can chew up Moreno's lead leg, everything else will grow easier.

Picking Moreno fights is no easy task. There's always a chance Moreno shows up looking like its 2022, and that version of "The Assassin Baby" would still be a title threat if he could show up consistently. Then, there's also a chance that Moreno shows up and falls over his own feet swinging his right hand — that guy is barely Top 15 .

Assuming we get something in the middle, it's hard not to favor the up-and-coming Morales. He has far fewer miles in the tank and has the power to hurt his opponent. If the two do end up on the mat, Morales' jiu-jitsu prowess should allow him to find his way to top position and spend more time overall in good position.

articles.title: No snap count restrictions for Chris Bell in Dolphins opener
articles.summary: Miami’s rookie receiver will be a full-go against Raiders in week one.
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins may have struck gold when they nabbed wide receiver Chris Bell from Louisville in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft. After all, the player was projected to be a late first round pick prior to his ACL tear in November of last year. Due to that injury, many thought that Bell would be eased back into action — possibly missing the first half of his rookie season. However, Bell's recovery has been an expeditious one, and the receiver has been named a starter for the Dolphins ahead of their Week One clash in Las Vegas against the Raiders .

And according to new head coach Jeff Hafley, Bell will be a full-go and will not be on a snap count when he takes the field on Sunday.

Yesterday, while speaking with the South Florida media, Hafley confirmed that Bell will have no restrictions against Las Vegas.

"We're going to play him — see how he feels — but, there's no pitch count on Chris."

Bell's full availability is an extremely positive development for the Dolphins, especially this early in the season. Quarterback Malik Willis will have a full complement of weapons for his first start with Miami — including fellow rookies Caleb Douglas and Kevin Coleman Jr., as well as Malik Washington and tight end Greg Dulcich . Of course, Miami's most explosive offensive player, De'Von Achane, will factor mightily into this tilt as well.

Will that be enough to allow Miami to sneak past Las Vegas? We will all find out in just a few short days.
